core_job: Pick a decade, find a film in the Internet Archive's public-domain and openly licensed film collections (Prelinger classroom and industrial films, Universal Newsreels, silent films, feature films), see what is in it, watch it, and keep your place. Every film shows its licence as the archive states it, plus a ready-made credit line. This is for teachers and students of history and media, video editors who need footage with a stated licence, and classic-film viewers who browse by era. It replaces the current Dailymotion-based YouTube look-alike. Search, Watch Later and resume all stay on the device, with no account. The data comes from keyless archive.org advancedsearch, metadata, thumbnail and MP4 endpoints, curl-checked on 2026-10-12. Baseline at the base sha: flutter analyze reported no issues and flutter test passed 389 tests.
signature: The Contact Sheet. A film's detail page shows a grid of real frames from the whole film, one every 30 seconds, each labelled with its timecode. The frames are the Internet Archive's own derived thumbnails (<id>.thumbs/<id>_NNNNNN.jpg, where NNNNNN is the second). Tapping a frame starts the film at that moment. A visible bookmark button on each frame saves a timecoded Moment to the Library, where it can be played, given a note, deleted or shared with a credit line. Verified on one item: HealthYo1953 has 22 frames, from second 1 to second 630. How many catalogue items have frames was not measured, so there is a 32-of-40 sampling gate before M3 is built. In their App Store listings, neither public-domain competitor (Eye Yay, id 6755102519; Eznetsoft OpenFlick, id 652389989) mentions a contact sheet, decade browsing or per-film licences. Eye Yay sells its bookmarks in a paid tier. Whether the apps actually lack these features was not verified.
